newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ex-communists launch election campaign.
newsitem.headline: Polish ex-communists launch election campaign.

text.p: The ruling ex-communists on Tuesday launched their election campaign by claiming credit for Poland's economic success and trotting out a "we have kept our word" slogan, which many analysts said may prove ineffective.

The Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) of ex-communists turned social democrats vowed to perserve financial stability, growth policies and efforts to bring Poland into the European Union and NATO if they win elections due in September.

"Back in 1993, opponents said our victory would bring about food rationing, queues, hyperinflation and that the West would turn its back on us," SLD's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz told a news conference.
"But changes went for the better in all spheres of social life. You have to be blind not to see them," he added.

Ex-communist leader Jozef Oleksy, also present, said his goal was to continue policies that resulted in growth of about six percent annually, a fall in inflation to 14.6 percent in May from nearly 40 percent in 1993 and billions of dollars in foreign investment.
"We aim to win the elections so as to govern in Poland. Our main policy line will be to safeguard growth, stabilise finances and solve social problems," Oleksy said.

The former communists, in a coalition with the Peasant Party (PSL) since 1993, are running neck-and-neck with the opposition Solidarity Election Action (AWS), a group of rightist parties clustered around the Solidarity trade union.
Both groups have more than 20 percent of support each and analysts say smaller parties are likely to hold a balance of power in the next parliament.

The Solidarity movement, which toppled communism in 1989 but lost power four years later due to internal quarrels, also vows market reforms but pledges to found them on honesty and patriotic, Christian values.
It alleges that many former communist activists are corrupt and their involvement in the oppressive regime before 1989 should disqualify them from politics.

Analysts said the slogan "We have kept our word" showed the SLD wanted the campaign to focus on specific policy issues, such as inflation or unemployment and divert the public's attention from more universal themes, such as historic or moral justice.

"The slogan shows the SLD wants to avoid discussions on broader themes, such as values, because they are not strong at them. They feel confident their concrete economic figures will speak for them," Halina Franczak, an analysts for the Demoskop polling institute, told Reuters.

"But this slogan is not a fortunate one. It invites the opposition to pinpoint areas in which the promises have not been kept and several such areas could be found," said Edmund Wnuk-Lipinski, a sociologist at the Polish Academy of Science.

The opposition charges that the left-wing coalition has failed to deliver on promises to reform the ailing social security system, reform the country's administration and hand over more power to local governments.
